claim: SC 2.2.1 requires content-set time limits to be turn-off-able, adjustable 10x, or extendable with a 20s warning; a timer needs no adjustment if a non-timed alternative to the information exists.
quote: Content that operates on a timer does not need to be time adjustable if there is an alternative that does not rely on a timer.

claim: Whether SC 2.2.1 applies to auto-dismissing toasts is an open W3C question raised by Patrick Lauke and still unresolved.
quote: While 4.1.3 Status Messages now at least ensures that, for AT users, the notification/toast should get announced explicitly (without moving focus), does a disappearing toast represent a timeout?

claim: SC 2.2.3 No Timing is Level AAA and requires timing not be an essential part of the activity.
quote: Timing is not an essential part of the event or activity presented by the content, except for non-interactive synchronized media and real-time events.

claim: SC 4.1.3 (Level AA) requires status messages to be programmatically determinable and announced without receiving focus.
quote: In content implemented using markup languages, status messages can be programmatically determined through role or properties such that they can be presented to the user by assistive technologies without receiving focus.

claim: The ARIA APG alert pattern has no keyboard interaction, must not move focus, and warns that auto-disappearing alerts can fail WCAG SC 2.2.3.
quote: Avoid designing alerts that disappear automatically. An alert that disappears too quickly can lead to failure to meet WCAG 2.0 success criterion 2.2.3.

claim: The APG's own alert example pre-renders an empty alert element and injects the message text into it.
quote: Activating the Trigger Alert button causes a message to be inserted into the example alert element.

claim: MDN states that dynamically adding an already-populated role=alert element generally produces no announcement, and that role=status should be used for non-urgent messages.
quote: Do not try to dynamically add/generate an element with role="alert" that is already populated with the alert message you want announced - this generally does not lead to an announcement, as it is not a content change.

claim: role=alert implies aria-live=assertive + aria-atomic=true, role=status implies polite; live region containers must be in the DOM before they are populated.
quote: place the live region container in the DOM as early as possible and then populate it with the contents of the message using JavaScript when the notification needs to be announced. This ensures that the live region is monitored for updates before they happen.

claim: Assertive announcements may clear queued polite messages; multiple DOM insertions cause double announcements; a 350-500ms blank-then-refill delay avoids duplicate announcements; aria-live is advisory only.
quote: Don't make multiple DOM insertions to create one message, otherwise the screen reader may make multiple separate message announcements

claim: A toast is a status message and belongs in role=status; virtual-cursor reading fires no focus event so focus-pause never helps SR users; toast actions must be duplicated in the primary document.
quote: A toast component should be considered a type of status message, and thus should be injected into a role="status".

claim: Lists the WCAG SCs toasts typically fail (1.3.2, 1.4.4, 1.4.10, 2.1.1, 2.2.1, 2.4.3, 3.2.4, 4.1.2, 4.1.3), argues live regions cannot carry interactive children, and notes GitHub removed toasts from its design system in late 2025 over accessibility issues.
quote: a screen reader will announce the raw text within, without any of the structure

claim: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 (AA) requires that a focused control not be entirely obscured by author-created content, which toast stacks can violate.
quote: Success Criterion 2.4.11 requires that interactive controls are not entirely obscured by author-created content, at the point when they receive focus.

claim: August 2025 teardown of Radix/React Aria/MUI/PrimeReact toast internals: NVDA does not announce a role=status element added already populated; Radix uses focus-proxy sentinels and a delayed re-render; React Aria uses F6/Shift+F6 landmark navigation; Radix and React Aria pause on window blur.
quote: If an element with role="status" is added to the page, its content will not be announced by NVDA.

claim: Open July 2025 issue: Radix Toast v1.2.14 renders aria-live="off" on the role=status element, so toasts are not announced by screen readers; reproduced in the official docs demo across Chrome, Safari and Firefox.
quote: When a toast is displayed, it's presence is not announced by screen readers due to the presence of aria-live="off" on the role="status" element.

claim: Radix Toast source: role=status always, aria-live switched assertive/polite by type; announce text rendered on the next frame for NVDA; default hotkey F8; viewport is role=region labelled with the hotkey.
quote: // Toasts are always role=status to avoid stuttering issues with role=alert in SRs.

claim: Radix Toast docs: F8 focuses the viewport, foreground toasts announced immediately (may clear queued messages), background at next opportunity; pauses closing on hover, focus and window blur.
quote: Pauses closing on hover, focus and window blur.

claim: Sonner previously rendered role=status only while a toast existed, so Windows Narrator and older iOS VoiceOver never announced toasts; closed via PR #436.
quote: ARIA live regions should always be present on screen so that screen readers can subscribe to their changes in order to announce future changes

claim: Sonner source: persistent section with aria-live=polite, aria-relevant=additions text, aria-atomic=false and no assertive/alert anywhere; TOAST_LIFETIME 4000ms; hotkey altKey+KeyT; container tabIndex -1, toasts tabIndex 0; pauses timer when expanded, interacting or document hidden.
quote: const TOAST_LIFETIME = 4000; ... aria-live="polite" aria-relevant="additions text" aria-atomic="false" ... hotkey = ['altKey', 'KeyT']

claim: Sonner ships a prefers-reduced-motion guard that disables all toast transitions and animations.
quote: @media (prefers-reduced-motion) { [data-sonner-toast], [data-sonner-toast] > *, .sonner-loading-bar { transition: none !important; animation: none !important; } }

claim: April 2026 shadcn/ui audit (WCAG 2.2 AA; NVDA + VoiceOver, Safari/Firefox/Chrome) flags Sonner's 4-second default auto-dismiss as a SC 2.2.1 failure and recommends 8s plus a close button.
quote: Sonner defaults to a 4-second auto-dismiss. For users with cognitive disabilities or slow readers, this is too fast.

claim: react-toastify defaults every toast to ARIA role alert, exposes an ariaLabel prop, and focuses the first toast on Alt+T.
quote: By default, all toasts are displayed with the ARIA role alert.

claim: Open issue: react-toastify toasts with role=alert are not announced in Firefox+Orca because the live region is created when the toast pops; fix is to put the role on an element present at page load.
quote: Do not try to dynamically add/generate an element with role="alert" that is already populated with the alert message you want announced - this generally does not lead to an announcement, as it is not a content change.

claim: react-toastify v11 (16 Dec 2024) added the ariaLabel prop and the Alt+T hotkey that focuses the first visible notification.
quote: If a notification is visible and the user presses alt+t it will focus on the first notification allowing the user to use Tab to navigate through the different elements within the notification.

claim: react-toastify's persistent container carries aria-live=polite, aria-relevant=additions text, aria-atomic=false; defaults are role 'alert', aria-label 'Notifications Alt+T', hotKeys altKey+KeyT focusing the first [tabIndex=0] toast.
quote: role: 'alert', 'aria-label': 'Notifications Alt+T', hotKeys: e => e.altKey && e.code === 'KeyT'

claim: Open issue (Jan 2024) asking react-hot-toast to fix its ARIA API: role=alert plus aria-live=assertive is redundant, and aria-live should be omitted when the role is alert.
quote: Since aria-role already functions as aria-live, it could be beneficial to eliminate ariaProps and structure it to allow passing only ariaRole as a toast option.

claim: react-hot-toast defaults ariaProps to { role: 'status', 'aria-live': 'polite' } and spreads them onto the Message element that mounts already containing its text; the Toaster renders plain divs with only onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave pause handlers and no hotkey or tabIndex.
quote: ariaProps: { role: 'status', 'aria-live': 'polite' }

claim: react-hot-toast default durations: blank 4000ms, error 4000ms, custom 4000ms, loading Infinity.
quote: blank: 4000, error: 4000, loading: Infinity, custom: 4000

claim: notistack sets role="alert" directly on the snackbar content element, which mounts already populated, for every variant including success and info; there is no persistent live region, no landmark and no hotkey.
quote: role="alert" aria-describedby={ariaDescribedby}

claim: React Aria Toast: toast regions are landmarks navigable with F6 / Shift+F6, focus is restored when the last toast closes, close button must be a sibling of the content, and auto-dismiss is discouraged for critical info with a 5s minimum.
quote: Only auto-dismiss toasts when the information is not critical, or may be found elsewhere. Some users may require additional time to read toasts, and screen zoom users may miss them entirely.

claim: Base UI Toast: F6 jumps into the toast viewport landmark, priority low/high maps to polite/urgent announcement, default timeout 5000ms with 0 disabling auto-dismiss, default limit 3.
quote: F6 lets users jump into the toast viewport landmark region to navigate toasts with keyboard focus.

claim: Base UI's toast viewport carries aria-live=polite / aria-atomic=false and renders a separate role="alert" aria-atomic region for high-priority toasts; a global F6 keydown force-focuses the viewport.
quote: 'aria-live': 'polite', 'aria-atomic': false ... <div key={toast.id} role="alert" aria-atomic>

claim: Base UI renders each toast root as a non-modal dialog, or alertdialog when priority is high, so interactive children remain reachable.
quote: role: isHighPriority ? 'alertdialog' : 'dialog'
